req_desc: Every object inside an array carries a permanent name assigned at creation ...
Every seeded person signs in with the password `deku-demo-pw-2026` ...
A contributor may not publish or unpublish a document ...
A denied publish leaves the published state untouched ...
`POST /api/auth/login` returns an opaque bearer access token ...
`GET /api/me` reports the signed-in person with their role plus their department ...
Role, department, grant are read from storage on every request rather than from the token.
`GET /api/datasets` returns each dataset with visibility, document count, asset count.
A document carries `_id`, `_type`, `_rev`, `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt` ...
A document created with a five-item array comes back with five distinct keys ...
`POST /api/data/mutate/{dataset}` accepts a client transaction identifier plus ordered mutations.
An editing surface sends a patch rather than a whole-document replacement.
A patch naming an array item by key lands on that item after a concurrent head insert.
A path addresses an array object through the key predicate form.
One hundred concurrent increments of one counter leave the counter at `100` ...
Replaying a transaction identifier inside `TRANSACTION_REPLAY_WINDOW_SEC` applies nothing ...
A revision mismatch is refused with the code `revision_mismatch` ...
A patch whose later operation is invalid applies none of its operations ...
Emboldening the middle of an unmarked span produces three spans ...
A span carries a key, text, a marks array.
Adjacent spans whose marks are equal as sets are merged ...
An orphaned `markDefs` entry is removed on the write that orphaned the entry.
An annotation is stored in `markDefs` under a key referenced from `marks` ...
Five consecutive bulleted blocks render as one list of five items.
A list is a run of adjacent blocks sharing one list marker.
Markup characters stored inside span text come back byte-identical ...
The `drafts` perspective returns a document under the published identifier ...
The draft identity is the published identity prefixed with `drafts.`.
`GET /api/data/history/{dataset}/{id}` returns every revision of the document ...
A read reports one of the four publication states the brief names ...
Unpublishing creates the draft plus removes the published document in one transaction ...
`GET /api/data/listen/{dataset}` opens with a welcome event ...
`POST /api/data/query/{dataset}` returns a result beside a cost record ...
A cost record carries the count of documents examined ...
A parameter carrying query syntax is treated as a literal string ...
A query exceeding a bound is refused with the code `query_bound_exceeded` ...
A migration invoked without `apply` writes nothing ...
Running one migration twice leaves the second run with nothing to change ...
A migration touching rich text keeps every surviving block key ...
A migration targeting `production` without the retyped name is refused with `production_confirmation_required` ...
Switching a dataset to `public` requires the dataset name typed again ...
A release publishes every member document in one transaction ...
A word split across spans by a mark is indexed as one word ...
`GET /api/search/{dataset}` answers an editor search over the dataset ...
An unmatched path returns `404` under the title `Page not found` ...
Every internal link on every public route resolves.
`GET /sitemap.xml` lists every public route ...
A recorded cookie decision survives a reload ...
A lead form submitted repeatedly in quick succession is refused ...
Search results are filtered against the caller's grants at query time.
A read carrying no credentials defaults to the `published` perspective ...
A draft-only article never appears on the blog index ...
A published-only caller asking for drafts receives published content with a stated downgrade ...
A mutation by query carrying no filter is refused with `unfiltered_mutation_refused` ...
Publishing with a draft-only strong dependency is refused with `publish_dependencies_unpublished` ...
Deleting a strongly referenced document is refused with `delete_blocked_by_references` ...
A dangling weak reference dereferences to null rather than raising.
A reference carries a target identifier plus a strength.
Uploaded bytes live in the bucket named by `STORAGE_BUCKET` under `assets/{dataset}/{sha256_of_bytes}.{ext}`.
An asset identifier embeds the content hash plus the dimensions ...
A derived rendering is cached under `derived/{dataset}/{sha256_of_bytes}/{parameter_digest}.{ext}`.
Changing one use's crop leaves every other use of that asset unchanged ...
A square rendering of an edge hotspot keeps the hotspot region fully visible.
A width beyond the original clamps rather than upscaling.
An asset in a private dataset is served only through the authenticated streaming endpoint.
A mislabelled upload is refused with the code `asset_type_refused` ...
The section rail carries the five numbered entries the brief names ...
The install command pill carries the command the brief names ...
A dataset's visibility is shown wherever the dataset is named.
Every code block names its language beside a copy control ...
`/pricing` serves the plans route ...
A refusal at sign-in is shown inline on the form ...
The document table shows one document per row under a shared header ...
The document editor is a single column of fields at a capped measure ...
Body copy on a published article is set at the body size the brief names.
Each image use shows its own alternative text beside the image ...
Every button wears the full capsule shape.
The brand colour renders as white on a dark surface.
The copy confirmation holds at the peak before settling ...
No content is hidden at any width except the install command pill ...
Two clients patching different items of one array both succeed ...
The replay window is read from `TRANSACTION_REPLAY_WINDOW_SEC`.
The server renders every route as markup before the browser receives the route ...
The revision, the history entry, the announcement record are written in one transaction.
No read reaches storage without a dataset predicate plus a grant predicate ...
One authorization decision is made per request before the body is validated ...
The audit chain verifies end to end after a hundred concurrent audited actions.
The document store together with the revision store form the permanent record.
A dataset row carries visibility, document count, asset count ...
The datasets `production` plus `staging` are seeded ...
A document row is unique on the dataset plus the identifier together ...
A transaction row is unique on the client-supplied identifier.
Every mutation produces a new revision identifier.
A revision row chains to the row before through a previous revision column.
A migration run row carries a mode defaulting to the dry run.
A release row carries its member document identifiers plus its state.
A lead row carries the work address, the name, the company, the team size.
A grant row carries a role, a dataset, a query filter.
The audit log is append-only, hash-chained, written through a single writer.
A reference edge row carries origin, target, path, strength.
An asset row is unique on the dataset plus the identifier together ...
The two very large closing actions are the ordinary button at a larger size.
No document of one department is visible to a person of another department, at any address ...
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready ...
Every list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array ...
No in-memory store substitutes for the datastore or the object store.
